case_title: State of Punjab v. Rakesh Kumar
statutory_provisions: NDPS Act s.8, s.22; Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.21 and s.22 of the NDPS Act
offence_finally_established: Violation of s.8 of the NDPS Act
neutral_facts: The accused was apprehended with a bulk quantity of manufactured drugs without any valid authorization. The trial court convicted him under sections 21 and 22 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985. The accused appealed, and during the pendency of the appeal, he sought suspension of sentence. The High Court allowed the application for suspension of sentence, but the Supreme Court set aside this order, finding that the accused should be tried under the NDPS Act rather than the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. The Supreme Court held that the NDPS Act is a special law aimed at curbing the usage of drugs for intoxication, while the Drugs and Cosmetics Act deals with sub-standard drugs for medicinal purposes. The accused was found to have violated section 8 of the NDPS Act, which prohibits possession of narcotic substances except for medical or scientific purposes.
